title: Edwin Lopez-Cornejo Dies at Delaney Hall; Third Death at Facility in Months
excerpt: Edwin Lopez-Cornejo, a 41-year-old Salvadoran detainee with diabetes, epilepsy, and high blood pressure, died at a Newark hospital after a medical emergency at Delaney Hall — the third death connected to the facility in less than a year, and the 24th in ICE custody in 2026.
content:
On August 1, 2026, Edwin Lopez-Cornejo, 41, a citizen of El Salvador who had lived in the United States for approximately two decades, died at University Hospital in Newark after suffering a medical emergency at the Delaney Hall ICE detention facility. He had been detained since June 18, 2026.

  • His mother reported that Lopez-Cornejo told her he had lost approximately 30 pounds during six weeks at Delaney Hall and was not receiving medication for his diabetes, high blood pressure, and epilepsy.
  • He described being held in a crowded cell with approximately 10 detainees sharing one open toilet.
  • His heart had already stopped beating when he arrived at the hospital, according to his mother.
  • Lopez-Cornejo was the third person known to have died after experiencing a medical emergency at Delaney Hall, and the second confirmed custody death at the facility within a year.

Newark Mayor Ras Baraka called the death "a heartbreaking reminder of the consequences of a facility that has operated for far too long without adequate oversight, accountability, or transparency." The death prompted New Jersey's attorney general to launch a civil rights investigation into the facility six days later.
